text: Rust also has two primitive types for _floating-point numbers_, which are numbers with decimal points. Rust’s floating-point types are `f32` and `f64`, which are 32 bits and 64 bits in size, respectively. The default type is `f64` because on modern CPUs, it’s roughly the same speed as `f32` but is capable of more precision. All floating-point types are signed. Here’s an example that shows floating-point numbers in action: Filename: src/main.rs ```rust {{#rustdoc_include ../listings/ch03-common-programming-concepts/no-listing-06-floating-point/src/main.rs}} ``` Floating-point numbers are represented according to the IEEE-754 standard.
